questions.question_text: Under RSA 331-A:26, which conduct is prohibited for NH licensees?
questions.explanation: RSA 331-A:26 lists prohibited conduct including misrepresentation, undisclosed dual agency, commingling, failure to account, paying unlicensed persons, inducing breach of contract, guaranteeing profits, and advertising violations.

questions.question_text: An agent tells a buyer the property will double in value within five years. Which prohibition does this violate?
questions.explanation: RSA 331-A:26 prohibits licensees from guaranteeing profits or making promises about future property values. Telling a buyer the property will double in value is a guarantee that violates this provision.

questions.question_text: A listing agent represents both buyer and seller without disclosing this to either party. Which violation occurred?
questions.explanation: RSA 331-A:26, XII prohibits acting for more than one party in a transaction without making full disclosure and obtaining the written consent of all parties, no later than the preparation of a written offer. An agent representing both buyer and seller must disclose and obtain written consent from both before proceeding.

questions.question_text: A broker pays a $500 referral fee to an unlicensed friend. Which NH law is violated?
questions.explanation: RSA 331-A:26, XXIV prohibits paying valuable consideration to any person not licensed under the chapter, with narrow exceptions for brokers licensed in another jurisdiction and licensee-owned entities under RSA 331-A:16-b. A referral fee is compensation for real estate services and may not be paid to an unlicensed person.

questions.question_text: A salesperson contacts a homeowner already under an exclusive listing with another firm, encouraging termination so the owner will relist with the salesperson's firm. What violation is this?
questions.explanation: RSA 331-A:26, XXXII prohibits inducing any party to a contract of sale or lease to break the contract in order to substitute a new contract with another principal. Soliciting a seller to terminate another firm's exclusive listing so the licensee can take the listing is the classic 'inducing breach of contract' violation, and such interference also demonstrates untrustworthiness under RSA 331-A:26, XXXVI.

questions.question_text: Under RSA 331-A:26, XVIII-XIX, what must NH licensees maintain for Commission inspection?
questions.explanation: RSA 331-A:26, XVIII requires escrow and trust account records to be kept for 3 years and made available to the Commission or its representatives on demand, and XIX requires a principal broker to preserve transaction records for 3 years after consummation. This ensures accountability and enables regulatory oversight.

questions.question_text: The Commission requests to examine a brokerage's transaction files. Can the broker refuse?
questions.correct_answer: No, Commission inspection access is required
distractors: Yes, if an attorney is present for review
Yes, unless an active complaint already exists
Only a formal court order compels access
questions.explanation: Under RSA 331-A:26, IX and XXXV, failing on demand to produce any document, book, or record for inspection and copying by the Commission or its authorized representatives is itself prohibited conduct. Trust account records must likewise be available to the Commission on demand under RSA 331-A:26, XVIII.

questions.question_text: Which provision of New Hampshire law sets the 3-year record retention requirements for brokerage records?
questions.explanation: RSA 331-A:26, XVIII requires records of escrow and trust accounts to be kept for 3 years and made available to the Commission on demand, and XIX requires a principal broker to preserve records of each real estate transaction for 3 years after consummation. Rea 702.02 covers delivery of funds by salespersons, RSA 331-A:13, V is the escrow audit permit, and Rea 404.04 governs brokerage contracts.

questions.question_text: A broker discovers old transaction files were accidentally destroyed. What risk does this create?
distractors: No consequence if the loss was unintentional
questions.explanation: Failure to maintain required records under RSA 331-A:26, XVIII-XIX — which require escrow account records and transaction records to be preserved for 3 years — is a potential violation regardless of intent. The broker should take steps to reconstruct the records where possible.

questions.question_text: A new salesperson asks what records must be kept. Under RSA 331-A:26, XVIII-XIX, who bears primary responsibility for the firm's records?
questions.correct_answer: The principal broker of the firm
questions.explanation: RSA 331-A:26, XVIII covers records of funds entrusted with the principal broker, and XIX makes it prohibited conduct for a principal broker to fail to preserve transaction records for 3 years. All licensees contribute records, but the principal broker is responsible for maintaining a compliant recordkeeping system.

questions.question_text: A licensee places an ad without identifying the brokerage name. What violation does this constitute?
distractors: Failure to deliver client funds promptly
questions.explanation: RSA 331-A:26 includes advertising violations as prohibited conduct. All real estate advertising must properly identify the licensed brokerage to prevent consumer confusion about who is offering the services.

questions.question_text: An agent mixes personal funds with a client's earnest money deposit. What is this violation called?
questions.explanation: Commingling occurs when a licensee mixes personal or business operating funds with client trust funds. RSA 331-A:13, I requires escrow funds to be kept separate and apart from the individual or office account, and RSA 331-A:26, VIII makes it prohibited conduct to fail to promptly place trust funds in a proper trust account.

questions.question_text: A broker fails to provide a client with an accounting of deposit funds when requested. Which prohibition applies?
questions.correct_answer: Failure to account for money received
distractors: Guaranteeing future profits to a client
questions.explanation: Under Rea 702.01(b), the principal broker is responsible to make full accounting of earnest money to the signatories of the contract, and RSA 331-A:26, VII treats failure to return entrusted money or documents within 30 days of demand as prima facie evidence of conversion. A broker must provide a prompt, accurate accounting when a client requests one.

questions.question_text: An agent knowingly inflates comparable sales data to justify a higher listing price. Which two violations most likely apply?
questions.correct_answer: Misrepresentation and failure to deal honestly
distractors: Commingling of funds and inducing breach
Advertising violation and paying unlicensed persons
Undisclosed dual agency and guaranteeing profits
questions.explanation: Knowingly providing false comparable sales data constitutes misrepresentation under RSA 331-A:26. It also reflects a failure to deal honestly in a transaction, potentially harming both the seller's realistic expectations and any buyer relying on inflated valuations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT prohibited under RSA 331-A:26?
distractors: Paying referral fees to unlicensed persons
questions.explanation: Representing clients in multiple transactions is a normal part of real estate practice and is not prohibited. RSA 331-A:26 targets specific harmful conduct such as commingling, guaranteeing profits, and compensating unlicensed individuals.
